title: Golden Dome faces 2027 funding cliff
summary: The Golden Dome program is at risk of a funding shortfall by 2027, with Gen. Michael Guetlein urging Congress to secure future financing as most initial funding has been allocated. The program's next phase remains uncertain without additional financial commitments.

title: National lab visit boosts NASA’s confidence in space nuclear propulsion mission
summary: NASA officials expressed confidence in launching a nuclear electric propulsion demonstration mission by the end of 2028 after visiting a national lab constructing the mission's reactor.

title: Golden Dome money starting to reach contractors, but long-term funding still unclear
summary: Pentagon contractors are starting to receive funding related to the Golden Dome initiative, but long-term financial commitments remain uncertain. Much of the allocated money is being funneled through existing programs.

title: Webinar on MOSA Interoperability Standards for Space Systems – August 26, 2026
summary: The MOSA Interface Standards Alliance is hosting a webinar on August 26, 2026, to discuss MOSA interoperability standards for space systems. The event aims to bring together industry stakeholders to promote standardization in space technology.

title: TechnoMile’s Five-Year Sustained Growth Recognized with  Place on the 2026 Inc. 5000 List
summary: TechnoMile, an AI solution provider for growth, contracts, compliance, and security workflows, has been ranked No. 4,268 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list. This recognition highlights its five-year sustained growth.

title: SpaceX increasing footprint in missile defense
summary: SpaceX is expanding its role in missile defense by securing multibillion-dollar contracts for satellite networks, sensing, and launch services, utilizing its vertically integrated manufacturing model to compete in Pentagon contracts.

title: Former Space Force general joins Lunar Outpost board
summary: A retired Space Force general, formerly the deputy commander of U.S. Space Command, has joined the board of lunar rover developer Lunar Outpost. This move highlights growing collaboration between military space leadership and commercial lunar exploration efforts.

title: BlackSky wins seven-figure, multiyear international contract
summary: BlackSky secured a seven-figure, multiyear international contract to provide persistent space-based monitoring and on-demand satellite tasking. The deal was announced on August 11.

title: Why Golden Dome Demands a Reimagined and Revitalized Industrial Base
summary: The article discusses the need for the U.S. to revitalize its industrial base, including the space sector, to counter foreign threats. It emphasizes the historical insulation of the U.S. due to its geography and the evolving nature of modern warfare.

title: First Neutron launch may slip to 2027
summary: Rocket Lab's first Neutron rocket launch may be delayed to 2027, as the chances of launching before the end of the year are becoming increasingly unlikely despite ongoing development progress.

title: SpaceX could make $500 billion in 2028, Elon Musk says
summary: SpaceX is projected to generate $500 billion in revenue by 2028, according to Elon Musk. The company, originally a launch provider, is expanding into artificial intelligence for future profits.

title: Scientists create largest 2D map of the universe with 5.6 trillion pixels and nearly 4 billion cosmic objects
summary: Scientists have developed the largest 2D map of the universe, containing 5.6 trillion pixels and nearly 4 billion cosmic objects. This achievement is expected to significantly advance astronomical research.

title: Scientists find 2 million active black holes, exploding stars and more, nearly doubling our view of the high-energy universe
summary: Astronomers have discovered 2 million active black holes and exploding stars, nearly doubling the known high-energy X-ray sources in the universe. This breakthrough significantly expands our view of the cosmos.

title: 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds': Anson Mount, Rebecca Romijn, & Carol Kane on season 4's big leaps and 'outside the box' episodes
summary: The producers of 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' had more time to prepare for season 4, resulting in incredible episodes. The cast discusses the show's big leaps and 'outside the box' storytelling.

title: 1-billion-year-old Mars meteorite found in Algeria is like nothing we've seen from the Red Planet
summary: Scientists discovered a 1-billion-year-old Martian meteorite in Algeria that provides new insights into the Red Planet's geological history. The meteorite fills a significant gap in Mars' geology timeline.

title: SpaceX launches 29 Starlink satellites to orbit from Florida (video, photos)
summary: SpaceX successfully launched 29 Starlink satellites into orbit from Florida's Space Coast. The mission marks another deployment in SpaceX's growing Starlink constellation.

title: NASA will chase the Aug. 12 total solar eclipse with balloons and a high-altitude jet
summary: NASA plans to observe the Aug. 12 total solar eclipse using balloons and a high-altitude jet to study the sun's corona. This approach offers unique insights not possible elsewhere in the solar system.

title: What history can teach us about the future of property rights in space (op-ed)
summary: The article discusses the importance of property rights in space for commercial development and settlement of celestial bodies. It highlights that without these rights, key economic incentives are missing.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 11, 1960: 1st object successfully recovered from orbit
summary: On August 11, 1960, the Discoverer 13 capsule became the first object successfully recovered from orbit. President Eisenhower inspected the capsule after its return to Earth.

title: Behold the majestic mane of the Lion Nebula | Space photo of the day for Aug. 11, 2026
summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captured a stunning image of the Lion Nebula, showcasing its glowing mane-like features. This space photo was featured as the daily highlight on August 11, 2026.

title: What Is the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope? (Grades 5-8)
summary: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is NASA's newest astrophysics observatory designed to scan large sections of space. It will help astronomers study dark energy, dark matter, and exoplanets.

title: NASA Completes Astronaut-Deployed Science Instrument for Lunar Surface
summary: NASA has completed the first science instrument designed for Artemis astronauts to deploy on the Moon's surface. The Lunar Environment Monitoring Station (LEMS) is now ready for deployment near the lunar South Pole.

title: Lion Nebula Roars in Webb’s Sights
summary: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope captured detailed images of NGC 2392, also known as the Lion Nebula, revealing its intricate 'mane' structure. The high-resolution images were released on August 10, 2026.

title: NASA Telescopes Create Colorful ‘Craft’ From Nearby Nebula
summary: NASA telescopes combined observations to create a colorful composite image of the Tarantula Nebula, revealing new details about the star-forming region. The image highlights the nebula's intricate structure within the Large Magellanic Cloud.

title: Building the Moon Base: NASA Stories at the Ion
summary: NASA's Moon Base Program is preparing for longer astronaut stays on the lunar surface, requiring new technologies and expertise. Shatel Bhakta, principal systems engineer, discussed challenges and opportunities at the Lunar South Pole during a presentation at NASA Stories at the Ion.

title: NASA Shares Station Research Today Supporting Moon, Mars Tomorrow
summary: NASA highlights ongoing research on the International Space Station in 2026, supporting future missions to the Moon and Mars. The Artemis II mission marked the first crewed lunar flyby in over 50 years.

title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 4968-4974: Rock Climbing Towards the Discontinuity
summary: NASA's Curiosity rover is exploring a large-scale erosional supersurface in Gale Crater, marking a significant geological transition. The mission, led by planetary scientist Lucy Lim, continues to study sedimentary records to understand Mars' past environmental changes.

title: APOD: 2026 August 11 – Six Moons of Saturn
summary: APOD features an image of six moons of Saturn. The Astronomy Picture of the Day highlights a different astronomical image daily with an explanation by a professional astronomer.

title: Bountiful Roebuck Bay
summary: Bountiful Roebuck Bay is a crescent-shaped bay in Western Australia's Kimberley region known for its tidal and seasonal shifts. The bay is recognized for its productivity and unique environmental characteristics.

title: Community College Instructors Bring Astronomy Textbook Into 21st Century
summary: Community college instructors are updating astronomy education by integrating modern resources and active learning strategies, with support from NASA.

title: Starbase Production lining up future vehicles

title: Blue Origin working engine resolutions and dual pad future
summary: Blue Origin is nearing the end of its investigation into a catastrophic engine explosion. The company is also planning for a dual-pad future.

title: Relativity Space engine integration milestone for Terran-R first stage
summary: Relativity Space achieved a key milestone by integrating engines into the first stage of its reusable Terran-R rocket. This advancement brings the company closer to its goal of developing a fully reusable launch vehicle.

summary: NASA has moved up the launch date for the Crew-13 mission to the ISS. A pilot reflects on their career, training, and upcoming scientific objectives ahead of the flight.

summary: SpaceX is recovering Ship 40 after its soft landing in the Indian Ocean, while Ship 41 prepares for testing ahead of Flight 14.

summary: The first full week of August is expected to be busy with multiple space missions, including launches by Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions. The launch manifest is filled with various activities.

summary: Boeing's CST-100 Starliner spacecraft may conduct a cargo mission to the ISS in 2026, following ongoing redesign efforts. Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg highlighted the progress in the spacecraft's development.

summary: SpaceX has conducted two flights from the newly designed Pad 2 at Starbase while retrofitting efforts continue for Pad 1. The transition to Block 3 flights marks a new phase in SpaceX's launch operations.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements. The publication marks five decades of the European Space Agency's contributions to space exploration and technology.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial missions and digital simulations to observe the Sun's corona, which is normally hidden by its bright disc. This approach allows scientists to gather more data than during brief natural eclipses.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard the Hera mission, which will travel millions of kilometers into deep space. This offers a unique chance to test software in a real deep-space environment.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency's technical center in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use a coronagraph to block the Sun's light, creating an artificial solar eclipse to study the Sun's corona. The mission involves two satellites playing a 'hide and seek' game to achieve this.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will showcase innovative space startups and foster collaboration with Europe's space industry. The two-day event at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands aims to exchange ideas and explore opportunities.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: The article discusses advancements in silicon-based technologies for next-generation antennas, which are crucial for space communications. These innovations are expected to enhance performance and efficiency in satellite and space mission operations.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: ESA's PLATO spacecraft has completed key electromagnetic compatibility tests in the Maxwell Test Chamber, confirming its electronics are fit for space. The mission is scheduled to launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Guetlein: CR Could Mean ‘No Golden Dome…No Funding’
summary: A senior official warned that a Continuing Resolution (CR) could lead to the cancellation of the 'Golden Dome' program due to lack of funding. The statement underscores the financial risks posed by budget uncertainty.

summary: Redwire subsidiary SpaceMD secured a contract to transport up to 32 mini-labs on a future SpaceX Starfall mission. This marks Redwire's first dedicated mission under the Starfall program.

title: Op-ed: Aging Weather Satellites Are Raising Risks for America. It’s Time for a Hybrid Solution.

summary: Rocket Lab faced investor scrutiny after releasing its second-quarter earnings, with a focus on its financial margins. The company's performance was closely analyzed by the space industry.

summary: The U.S. Space Force has selected Voyager Technologies to develop space-to-space communication capabilities under a new contract. This award marks a significant step in enhancing military communications in space.

summary: The Trump Administration nominated a fourth member for the FCC, currently operating with three members, ahead of the midterm elections. The nomination aims to fill an empty seat at the Federal Communications Commission.

title: Arabsat Signs Digital Communications Infrastructure Deal with Libya Telecom and Technology (LTT)
summary: Arabsat has signed a deal with Libya Telecom and Technology (LTT) to develop Libya's digital communications infrastructure. The agreement aims to enhance connectivity for Libya's population of approximately 7.5 million people.

title: ALL.SPACE to Provide Hydra MAX Terminals to Aalyria
summary: ALL.SPACE has secured a contract to supply Hydra MAX terminals to Aalyria, which will be integrated with Aalyria's Spacetime orchestration software. The collaboration aims to enhance Aalyria's platform capabilities.

title: Catalyst Completes Infrastructure EO Analysis Pilot Program with UK Rail Operator
summary: Catalyst (PCI Geomatics) completed a 12-week pilot program with Network Rail to analyze weather-driven risks using Earth Observation (EO) analytics. The program focused on infrastructure EO analysis for Britain's railway network.

title: SES, Eutelsat Complete RDV1 Milestone for Europe’s IRIS2 Sovereign Constellation Program
summary: SES and Eutelsat have achieved the RDV1 milestone for Europe's IRIS² sovereign constellation program. This marks a significant step in the implementation phase of the initiative.

title: CEO Fallacher Suggests Eutelsat is ‘Undervalued’ Compared to SpaceX Following 2025-26 Results
summary: Eutelsat reported strong growth in its LEO business segment for the 2025-2026 fiscal year. CEO Fallacher suggested the company is undervalued compared to SpaceX.

title: How the Internet of Space is Reshaping Active Resiliency
summary: Satellite data is crucial for disaster assessment and emergency response, with the Internet of Space enhancing active resiliency. The article highlights the long-term impact of satellite technology in understanding disaster impacts.
